bib.title: Long Short-Term Memory-Networks for Machine Reading
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 2016 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), pages 551-561

question: How can a sequence-level recurrent network be made better at handling structured input by inducing latent relations among tokens and memorising longer sequences?
hypothesis: Replacing the LSTM's single memory cell with a memory network read by intra-attention at every step lets the network store each token's representation without compression and induce soft token relations, beating vanilla LSTMs.
contributions: LSTMN: an LSTM whose single memory cell is replaced by a memory tape (one slot per token) addressed by intra-attention at each step, giving non-Markov state updates
Two ways (shallow and deep attention fusion) to combine intra-attention with encoder-decoder inter-attention for two-sequence tasks
Experiments on language modeling, sentiment analysis and natural language inference

method.summary: The LSTMN keeps a hidden tape and a memory tape with one slot per processed token. At each step an attention layer over previous hidden states yields a weighted summary of past hidden and memory vectors that replaces h(t-1), c(t-1) in the LSTM update. For two sequences, shallow fusion uses LSTMNs as encoder and decoder with inter-attention, and deep fusion also stores the inter-attention vector in the target memory through a gate.
method.task: language modeling (Penn Treebank), sentence sentiment classification (Stanford Sentiment Treebank), natural language inference (SNLI)

datasets.name: Penn Treebank
datasets.size: about 1M tokens, vocabulary 10K, average sentence length 21
datasets.split: sections 0-20 train (1M words), 21-22 validation (80K words), 23-24 test (90K words)
datasets.source: English Penn Treebank, following Mikolov et al. (2010)

datasets.name: Stanford Sentiment Treebank
datasets.split: fine-grained: 8,544 train / 1,101 validation / 2,210 test; binary (neutral removed): 6,920 / 872 / 1,821

datasets.name: SNLI
datasets.size: 549,367 train pairs, 9,842 dev, 9,824 test; vocabulary 36,809; average sentence length 22
datasets.preprocessing: lower-casing and tokenization of the entire dataset

models.name: LSTMN
models.architecture: LSTM with memory tape and intra-attention; 1 or 3 layers for LM, 1 or 2 layers for sentiment
models.init_from: word embeddings from GloVe 840B 300-D for sentiment and SNLI; random for LM
models.context: memory grows with time up to an upper bound of the memory span (bound not stated)

models.name: KN5, RNN, LSTM, sLSTM, gLSTM, dLSTM
models.architecture: Kneser-Ney 5-gram; RNN; LSTM; stacked LSTM; gated-feedback LSTM (Chung 2015); depth-gated LSTM (Yao 2015)

other.note: KN5 and RNN perplexities taken from Mikolov et al. (2015)

training.objective: language modeling: negative log likelihood; sentiment and NLI: task classification loss (not named), trained end-to-end with no direct supervision of attention
training.optimizer: LM: SGD; sentiment and NLI: Adam with momentum 0.9 and 0.999
training.lr_schedule: LM: decays by a factor of 0.85 per epoch if no significant improvement on validation; others not stated
training.dropout: sentiment: 0.5 on the classifier; SNLI: selected from [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4]; LM: not stated
training.regularisation: gradient renormalised if norm greater than 5 (LM); GloVe-initialised word gradients scaled by 0.35 in first epoch (sentiment); only OOV vectors updated in first epoch (SNLI)

other.sentiment_classifier: averaged hidden vector passed to a 2-layer neural network classifier with ReLU
other.snli_classifier: average pooling of each LSTMN hidden tape, concatenate, 2-layer ReLU classifier

inference.samples: single run per configuration implied; not stated

metrics.name: Perplexity
metrics.definition: PPL = exp(NLL/T), NLL of the entire test set, T number of test tokens

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: classification accuracy on test set (sentiment fine-grained 5-class and binary; SNLI 3-way)

eval.protocol: Test-set numbers reported once; no seeds, variance or significance tests stated.

results.claim: Attention concentrates on recent memories, consistent with long-range dependencies being rare, while some valid lexical relations are captured (qualitative).

results.quote: much attention focuses on recent memories. This agrees with the linguistic intuition that long-term dependencies are relatively rare.

limits: The SNLI state-of-the-art claim is confounded by parameter count; authors say the result should be interpreted with caution and do not run a parameter-matched comparison.
No seeds, variance or significance tests; no compute, hardware or training time reported; epochs not stated.
Only the read operation of memory is implemented; write is left for future work.
Intra-attention relations are undirected and weakly induced with no supervision; the paper gives only qualitative attention examples as evidence of structure.
Sequential recurrence with attention over all prior states; cost scaling is not discussed. Superseded by the Transformer (self-attention without recurrence).

terms.definition: Long Short-Term Memory-Network: an LSTM whose memory cell is replaced by a memory network storing each token's contextual representation in a unique slot
attention over the model's own previous hidden states within a sequence, used for memory addressing and to induce relations among tokens
shallow: LSTMN as drop-in encoder and decoder with inter-attention; deep: inter- and intra-attention combined in the state update with the inter-alignment vector stored in target memory

lineage.note: memory network replaces LSTM memory cell
lineage.quote: replacing the memory cell with a memory network (Weston et al., 2015)

lineage.work: Neural machine translation by jointly learning to align and translate (Bahdanau et al.)
Reasoning about entailment with neural attention (Rocktaschel et al.)
Learning natural language inference with LSTM (Wang and Jiang)
